endorsements.quote: It is advisable to nominate a governance body that oversees the lifecycle management of the AI system and determines accountable persons for the respective lifecycle phases.
There should be measures in place to intervene or even disable an AI system if necessary.

A risk assessment should be performed for each AI system aimed at supporting pharmacovigilance processes and should form the basis for a risk-proportionate approach applied throughout the AI system’s lifecycle from development to routine use.
The risk strategy should be reviewed and adapted as needed at regular pre-planned intervals, or whenever the AI system shows performance issues.
Ideally, organisations should conduct data protection impact assessments prior to deployment to identify and mitigate risks inherent in data processing.

Data processing must align with legislation such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in the European Union (EU) or the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) in the United States.
When using AI systems, pharmacovigilance professionals should be aware of pitfalls such as automation bias or confirmation bias [14].
The report refers to the importance of evaluating and documenting data representation.

unlisted_practices: Integrate AI systems deployed in critical pharmacovigilance processes into the organisation's business continuity plan so safety monitoring and compliance continue if the system is unavailable or degrades.
Document AI components supporting pharmacovigilance activities in the Pharmacovigilance System Master File where PSMF-based requirements apply.
Disclose AI use to affected stakeholders, including its intended use, human-computer interaction, training and validation data, and known limitations.
Disclose AI performance evaluation details, including the nature, size, and diversity of test sets and their alignment with the intended deployment domain.
Use large, diverse test sets and subgroup and sensitivity analyses to evaluate AI generalisability, bias, and fairness.
Complement statistical AI performance evaluation with qualitative review of individual model outputs.
Clearly define the intended use and deployment domain of AI solutions and target performance evaluation to them.
Ensure pharmacovigilance professionals and decision makers can critically appraise AI systems, whether developed in-house or procured.
Provide training, change management, and readiness strategies for staff in AI oversight roles.
Deploy generative LLMs handling sensitive data in private clouds within institutional firewalls rather than publicly hosted environments.
Apply data minimisation, anonymisation, and encryption to pharmacovigilance data used in AI systems.
Maintain traceability and version control of AI systems throughout their lifecycle.

screen.reason: Presents guiding principles and governance recommendations from the CIOMS Working Group XIV for the responsible use of AI in pharmacovigilance.
